title: One SunPath Solar Lease per Home: Signing and Assumption Rule
content:
Under the SunPath Solar Lease a home carries one lease at a time. The rule governs two moments: signing a lease, and a lease passing to the buyer when the home is sold.

## 1. Signing

> A lease is signed only for a purchase agreement with no other lease in status pending installation, pending PTO or active.

**Pending installation** is a signed lease whose system is not yet installed; **pending PTO** is a lease whose system is installed and awaits the utility's permission to operate; **active** is a lease whose term has begun.

- **What decides it.** The company's own lease records decide the point, not the customer's account of them. The check is made before the lease is signed.
- **Which object.** The leases that count are those recorded against the same purchase agreement as the lease being signed. Leases on the customer's other purchase agreements do not count against this one.

| Status of another lease recorded on the same purchase agreement | Effect under this rule |
|---|---|
| Pending installation | A lease is not signed for that purchase agreement |
| Pending PTO | A lease is not signed for that purchase agreement |
| Active | A lease is not signed for that purchase agreement |
| Transferred, bought out or terminated | Not a bar under this rule |
| No other lease recorded | Not a bar under this rule |

## 2. Transfer on a sale of the home

On a transfer, the buyer of the home signs a new lease for the remaining term on the same system, and the seller's lease becomes **transferred**. The seller's lease leaves the active status at that point, and the buyer's new lease covers the same system for what remains of the term.

## Hypothetical cases

- A purchase agreement has one lease recorded on it whose status is active. A second lease for that purchase agreement is not signed.
- A purchase agreement has one lease recorded on it whose status is terminated, because the earlier home purchase did not close. That terminated lease is not a bar under this rule.
- A customer has an active lease on one purchase agreement and asks for a lease on a different purchase agreement with no lease recorded on it. The active lease on the first agreement is not a bar to the second, because only leases on the same purchase agreement count.
